62.notes: 1,303± contiguous acre legacy ranch in the historic Clear Creek Valley of North Texas, assembled over nearly 30 years by the current owner with homes, trails, and scenic overlooks; emphasis on stewardship and wildlife habitat. New listing, $16,500/acre, minerals conveyed to buyer.

63.name: Greenwood County Ranch
63.water_features: Multiple water sources across the ranch (ponds/wells per listing summary, not itemized)
63.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement language found in available listing summary; full brokerage page not accessible to confirm.
63.notes: 1,086-acre turnkey Flint Hills cattle ranch near Toronto, KS with established cattle income, strong wildlife habitat, and multiple water sources in a high-demand recreational corridor. Notable for Tallgrass Prairie region positioning and income-producing cattle operation.

64.name: Rimrock Ranch
64.water_features: Seasonal draws/runoff; no major river frontage noted
64.conservation_easement_notes: No mention of a conservation easement in listing materials reviewed (Land and Farm, Western Ranch Brokers, AcreValue); status cannot be confirmed either way.
64.notes: 1,495± total acres (1,455± deeded, 40± BLM) in the Billings-to-Red Lodge corridor, defined by a namesake rimrock formation, native grasslands and pine timber. Strong elk/mule deer/antelope habitat, 40 min from both Billings and Red Lodge; adjacent 120-acre inholding available separately for $225,000.

65.name: Whitney Ranch
65.conservation_easement_notes: Hall and Hall brochure makes no mention of an easement; status cannot be confirmed either way.
65.notes: 1,284± deeded acres near Crawford, Nebraska, split between 500± dryland hay acres and 784± native grassland. All-new exterior fencing, good Highway 20 and county-road access; straightforward working cattle ranch at an attractive entry price.

66.name: Comanche Ridge Game Ranch
66.conservation_easement_notes: No mention of a conservation easement across Fay Ranches, Republic Ranches, or Farm & Ranch listing copy reviewed; status cannot be confirmed either way.
66.notes: 737± high-fenced acres near Sidney, TX managing bison, elk, blackbuck, oryx, axis deer and whitetail alongside cattle. 2,139 sq ft 2007 stone home on a high point overlooking one of three lakes; ~139 mi from Fort Worth.

67.name: Whitehall Ranch Homestead
67.water_features: Spring-fed creek, 8± acre lake managed for trophy bass
67.conservation_easement_notes: No mention of a conservation easement in listing materials reviewed; status cannot be confirmed either way.
67.notes: 656± acres in southern Grimes County, 12 mi south of Navasota and 61 mi from Houston, with 3,000+ ft of CR 305 road frontage. Architect-designed main home, spring-fed creek through oak/pecan bottoms, pine forest, and an 8-acre trophy bass lake — turnkey luxury ranch estate.

68.name: Piney Ridge Ranch
68.conservation_easement_notes: No mention of a conservation easement for this specific ranch in listing materials reviewed (distinct from nearby 'Creek Bend Ranch', which does carry one); status cannot be confirmed either way.
68.notes: 2,099.43± deeded acres in the western Black Hills near Sundance/Upton, WY, plus 1,279± acres of State and Forest Service leases. 6,500 sq ft custom log home, heated indoor arena, cow/calf operation rated for 225 pairs, and two landowner elk tags issued yearly.

69.name: C100 Tanager ET2-2031
69.water_features: ~3,000 ft frontage near tidal creek system off Rt. 14
69.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned for this tract; a nearby unrelated Advance Land and Timber listing (B949 Devils Gut Tract) does carry a partial easement, but no such language appears for Tanager 2031. Status cannot be confirmed either way.
69.notes: 2,120± acre managed timberland tract 6.5 mi north of Gloucester, VA, across eight tax parcels zoned agricultural. 1,630 ac planted loblolly pine, 287 ac natural loblolly, 186 ac mature hardwoods; pine sawtimber is 54% of total volume. Access via prescriptive easement off Rt. 14.

70.name: 5250-Acre Wilderness Ranch
70.water_features: 1+ mile of accessible Kiamichi River frontage
70.conservation_easement_notes: Listing explicitly confirms an existing conservation easement 'in place on the majority of the property,' put in place to protect water quality flowing into Lake Eucha (Tulsa's water supply); listing states it is not restrictive to hunting, recreation, or land management.
70.notes: 5,250± acres (8+ sq mi) near Antlers, OK with hardwood/pine timber including 500+ acres of structured pine plantation, elevations from 400' to 980', and 1+ mile of Kiamichi River frontage. Managed for both recreation (hunting, fishing, kayaking) and timber production; majority of acreage under a water-quality conservation easement that doesn't restrict recreational use.

71.name: Judith River Confluence Ranch
71.water_features: Where Sage Creek meets the Judith River; ~86± irrigated acres with valuable irrigation water rights
71.conservation_easement_notes: Land & Farm listing explicitly states 'No conservation easements' for this property.
71.notes: 2,263± total acres (1,783± deeded + 480± State lease) at the confluence of Sage Creek and the Judith River in Central Montana. Offered as a continuous block with productive farm ground, grazing, and strong recreational/scenic value.

72.name: Beartooth Canyon Ranch
72.water_features: Headwaters of Sheep Creek and Midnight Creek; Meadow Creek trout fishing; Antelope Creek Ditch irrigation rights on ~40 acres
72.conservation_easement_notes: Listing explicitly states property is 'not encumbered by a conservation easement' and highlights 'no conservation easement in place' as a selling point, while noting a future easement could be established if desired.
72.notes: 2,797± deeded acres (3,047± total incl. State lease) at the foot of the Beartooth Mountains near Nye, MT. Former oil exploration infrastructure fully removed/reclaimed; two rustic cabins, strong elk/big game hunting, creek frontage on every parcel.

73.name: The Great Falls Place Ranch
73.water_features: Beaver Creek corridor; located in Milk River Valley; 1,038.9± hayable acres
73.conservation_easement_notes: Listing discusses only a hypothetical future 'conservation potential' / possible easement for conservation-minded buyers; no current easement is mentioned or in place, so treated as not currently encumbered.
73.notes: 1,193.74± contiguous deeded acres between Malta and Saco in Montana's Milk River Valley, long farmed by the Menge and Barnard families. Highly productive irrigated hay/farm ground along the Beaver Creek corridor with strong wildlife habitat value.

74.name: 1897 James River Ranch
74.water_features: Spring-fed James River frontage with deep pools and fertile bottomland
74.mineral_rights: Owned minerals negotiable; mineral ownership otherwise unknown, no current production
74.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement language found in listing materials; neighboring land is noted as 'conservation land' but no easement on the subject tract is confirmed either way.
74.notes: 1,290± acres along the James River south of Mason, TX, in the same family since 1897. Dramatic elevation changes, deep river pools, diverse wildlife; marketed as a blank-canvas legacy ranch for recreation or livestock.

75.name: Lost Creek Ranch
75.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned in listing materials (HAR data lists only a utility/electric easement); status not confirmed either way.
75.notes: 521.45± acre game-fenced managed wildlife property in Northeast Texas near Linden. Rolling terrain, mature hardwoods and pine timber, natural springs, trophy whitetail breeding program infrastructure, feeders/blinds/camera systems, and introduced Rio Grande turkeys.

76.name: The Stephens Ranch on Bluff Creek
76.water_features: Bluff Creek runs through the property for nearly 1.5± miles, year-round water source
76.conservation_easement_notes: Listing lists 'easements' among items 'subject to verification by all Buyers' but does not confirm presence or absence of a conservation easement specifically.
76.notes: 3,722± acre legacy ranch homesteaded in 1885, in the Stephens family for 140+ years, offered to the public for the first time. Combines premier whitetail/mule deer hunting habitat (Deer Management Unit 16), productive farmland, and quality grazing pasture along Bluff Creek near Ashland, KS.

77.name: The Eagle Retreat
77.source: Land And Farm / FRC Land Company
77.water_features: Creeks and ponds within 1,000+ acre tract (southeast GA)
77.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned in listing marketing materials found; status unconfirmed.
77.notes: 1,005± contiguous acres, one of the largest single tracts in Bulloch County, GA. Mix of recreational, timberland and hunting land roughly 90 min from Savannah. Notable for scale in a county where tracts this size rarely trade.

78.name: Promised Land Whitetail Ranch
78.water_features: River bottom frontage and abundant internal water features
78.conservation_easement_notes: Listing explicitly states 'no conservation easement for total flexibility' and markets the property as 'unrestricted for future use or development.'
78.notes: 1,583± acre high-fence whitetail operation with established deer management program, hardwoods/pine/pasture/river bottom mix. ~90 min to Port of Savannah and near the Kia EV plant corridor, adding development upside given confirmed easement-free status.

79.name: Hughes Creek Plantation
79.water_features: Hughes Creek and Tallahaga Creek run through property
79.mineral_rights: Minerals available to convey with sale
79.conservation_easement_notes: National Land Realty listing brochure explicitly states 'No Easement Encumbrances.'
79.notes: 2,464± contiguous acres first offered to the public in over 40 years. Mix of row crop, CRP (394.5 acres under contracts through 2031), and pasture, 30 min to Starkville and 1 hr to Jackson metro. Minerals convey, no easement restrictions — notable combination for a large contiguous Deep South tract.

80.name: M Spear Ranch
80.water_features: 20 tire tanks and three wells distributed across the ranch
80.conservation_easement_notes: Hall and Hall listing does not mention an easement (unlike the similar nearby Go Away Ranch, which is explicitly eased); status not confirmed either way.
80.notes: 7,307± deeded acre working cattle ranch 30 minutes from Lusk, WY, with a 3,744± sq ft residence and a 1,065± sq ft cabin. Well-watered across the full acreage via tire tanks and wells — a large-scale, amply improved grazing operation.

81.name: Spread Oaks Ranch
81.water_features: Miles of Colorado River frontage, Blue Creek, Jennings Lake, stocked lakes, ~25 wells, 1,443 acre-feet of Blue Creek water rights
81.conservation_easement_notes: Owner donated a conservation easement to Coastal Prairie Conservation in 2017; confirmed in place. Easement is structured to allow continued agricultural, cattle, and commercial lodge operations, not a hard development freeze.
81.notes: 5,300± acre Gulf Coast sporting and agricultural estate along the Colorado River at the top of the Central Flyway — world-class duck hunting, active Brangus cattle program, farming income, and a commercial hunting lodge. Under a working conservation easement that preserves ag/commercial flexibility. One of the largest and highest-priced new listings tracked this month.

82.name: 10 Shy Ranch and Timber
82.conservation_easement_notes: No easement mentioned in brochure or marketing materials found; status unconfirmed.
82.notes: 2,290± mainly contiguous acres across Henry and Barbour Counties in Alabama's Wiregrass region, with 1,217+ acres of loblolly pine plantation plus pastureland. Income potential from cattle, timber, pine straw, and hunting leases; 9.65 miles of road frontage across seven county roads.

83.name: Franklin Farms - Franklin County
83.source: Land And Farm / All Things Land Company
83.conservation_easement_notes: No easement mentioned in listing description found; status unconfirmed.
83.notes: 2,723± acre large-scale timberland/farm/hunting tract in northwest Alabama with over five miles of road frontage. One of the biggest contiguous offerings to hit the Alabama market this cycle.

84.name: Beaverkill Forest
84.water_features: Over a mile of frontage along the Beaverkill River in the Catskills
84.conservation_easement_notes: Listing markets 'conservation benefits' and future conservation/development potential as a selling point but does not confirm an existing recorded easement in place today; treated as unknown rather than assumed true or false.
84.notes: 1,184± acre Catskills timber tract between Hancock and Roscoe, NY, with standing timber valued at $1,685,300 per 2024 inventory. Notable Northeast river-frontage timberland play with both near-term timber income and longer-term development/conservation optionality.

85.name: Rockin R Ranch
85.water_features: Extraordinary water resources per listing; exact feature not itemized
85.mineral_rights: All mineral rights intact and transfer with the property
85.conservation_easement_notes: Listing emphasizes wildlife/genetic conservation program (captive breeding) but does not mention a recorded land conservation easement; status unconfirmed.
85.notes: 600± acre high-fence sporting estate in Kansas's Flint Hills (440 acres high-fenced for exotic/big-game hunting, 160 acres leased for cattle grazing). Luxury barndominium residence, dramatic elevation changes and native grassland — notable for scale of improvements on a sub-1,000 acre Midwest tract; all minerals convey.

86.name: Heaven's Farm and Ranch
86.water_features: Six center-pivot irrigation systems over the Ogallala Aquifer irrigating 1,023± acres
86.conservation_easement_notes: No easement mentioned in listing; status unconfirmed.
86.notes: 2,279± contiguous acre irrigated cattle ranch 15 miles north of Scottsbluff, NE, over the Ogallala Aquifer. Six-pivot system supports ~2,000 head with additional quarry revenue — an investment-grade, self-sustaining forage operation rarely offered at this scale in the Panhandle.

87.name: RC Ranch
87.water_features: Over 20 miles of Rock Creek frontage running through the ranch, 15+ reservoirs/stock ponds, territorial water rights supporting 1,930± flood-irrigated acres
87.mineral_rights: Any mineral rights owned by the seller transfer to the buyer; no current oil/gas production on the ranch
87.conservation_easement_notes: Detailed listing covers water rights, mineral rights, and general operations sections in depth but makes no mention of a conservation easement either way; status not determinable from available listing material.
87.notes: 22,657± total acre (17,223± deeded, plus BLM/State lease) well-blocked Wyoming cattle operation 44 miles northwest of Laramie. Supports 1,200-1,300 cow/calf pairs or 2,000+ yearling stockers with over 20 miles of Rock Creek and strong mule deer/antelope hunting.

88.name: White River Ranch
88.water_features: White River flows through the SE corner feeding sub-irrigated meadows; 53.9± acres of adjudicated surface water rights (permits A-4420AR/BR, priority date 1949); Gorr Reservoir plus multiple stock ponds
88.mineral_rights: All owned mineral rights convey to the buyer
88.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned anywhere in the multiple listing sources reviewed (LandWatch, Land.com, Luxury Ranch Real Estate); status unconfirmed.
88.notes: 5,888.56± contiguous acres, a large well-managed grazing operation with abundant sub-irrigated river meadows, strong Hwy 385 access, and a workable building site near Chadron. Notable for scale and water resources in the Nebraska Panhandle.

89.name: Niobrara River Ranch
89.water_features: Over 3 miles of Niobrara River frontage; 134± acres of adjudicated water rights with 125± acres under a 7-tower 1999 Zimmatic pivot; windmills, pipeline tanks, and solar-powered wells
89.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned in listing marketing materials reviewed; status unconfirmed.
89.notes: 4,080± acre Cherry County ranch blending native grassland pasture with irrigated cropland along more than 3 miles of the Niobrara River, in the nation's top cattle-producing county. Strong livestock water plus recreational/hunting upside (deer, upland birds, waterfowl).

90.name: 1,704.7 Acre Comanche County Hunting Land (Kansas Trophy Hunting Ranch)
90.water_features: Multiple ponds distributed across the property
90.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned in listing description found across Whitetail Properties, Land & Farm, and Land.com sources; status unconfirmed.
90.notes: 1,704.7± acres along the Comanche/Kiowa County line blending productive grassland, tillable fields, timbered draws, multiple ponds, and an updated residence with exceptional operational improvements — a versatile production/recreation ranch in KS Deer Management Unit 16 country.

91.name: Knudtson Farm
91.water_features: Over 2 miles of Rock River frontage; property protected by an Army Corps of Engineers-maintained levee
91.conservation_easement_notes: 63.28 acres are enrolled in the federal Conservation Reserve Program (CRP), which is a temporary (10-15 yr) paid set-aside contract, NOT a permanent conservation easement. No actual recorded conservation easement is mentioned anywhere in the listing; the brochure actively markets 'significant future development upside' and 'strong solar development potential,' suggesting the land is unrestricted, but this is not an explicit statement either way, so left as unknown rather than assumed false.
91.notes: 570± acre (also offered in 669.82-acre configuration) investor-grade Rock Island County farm with 409.43 FSA cropland acres at PI 132.2, never-logged mature timber along the Rock River, and strong solar development potential given nearby substation access — a notable Midwest row-crop/river-frontage/1031-exchange play just east of the Quad Cities.

92.name: Drinkuth Lane Kingdom Lot
92.conservation_easement_notes: No conservation easement mentioned; marketed as an undeveloped 'kingdom lot' with sufficient timber stocking to pay taxes, which suggests unrestricted status, but this isn't an explicit statement either way.
92.notes: 2,716± acre Western Maine mountain timber tract spanning the Webb River, hardwood ridges, sugar maple forests, and spruce-fir stands. A rare large unbroken Northeast timberland offering with standing timber value sufficient to cover carrying costs.

93.name: Eden's Echo Forest
93.conservation_easement_notes: CONFIRMED existing easement: protected by two Vermont Land Trust conservation easements (one covering land north of East Hill Road, one south), recorded in perpetuity, explicitly permitting sustainable forestry and sugaring but restricting development outside ~24 acres of carved-out development zones.
93.notes: 1,701± acre northern Vermont timberland and maple sugaring investment in the Northeast Kingdom, with an established sugarhouse (~30,000 taps on 565± acres, room for 12,000 more) and mature mixed-wood timber. Under a permanent Vermont Land Trust conservation easement that preserves working-forest/sugarbush use while limiting development to small carve-out zones.

94.name: Neosho River Hunting Mecca
94.water_features: Over 2 miles of Neosho River frontage; ~290 acres of diked wetlands with 15 water control structures across 15 pools
94.conservation_easement_notes: Listing explicitly markets the property as a '754± acre WRP farm' — enrollment in USDA's Wetlands Reserve Program requires granting a conservation easement to NRCS (permanent or 30-year) over the enrolled wetland acreage (~290± acres here). Treated as a confirmed existing easement over that portion of the tract; exact easement term (permanent vs. 30-yr) and precise encumbered acreage are not stated in the listing itself.
94.notes: 754± acre Neosho County hunting farm near the renowned Neosho Wildlife Area, with over 2 miles of river frontage, ~290 acres of diked WRP wetlands holding thousands of wintering ducks/geese, large hardwood timber bottoms, and native grass stands for deer and turkey. The WRP wetland acreage carries a confirmed conservation easement.
